name: Alaska
tagline: Inside Passage ferries, a flag-stop railroad and gravel highways reaching toward the Arctic Ocean.
intro: Alaska's byways go by ferry from the Inside Passage out to the Aleutians and by rail from Seward to Fairbanks, while its highways run from the Homer Spit north over the Brooks Range almost to the Arctic Ocean. This chapter follows the Alaska Scenic Byways Program, established in 1993 and run by the Alaska Department of Transportation and Public Facilities. The state designates a ferry system, a railroad and a boat crossing alongside its roads, and it lists the Richardson and Sterling highways as separate north and south segments with undesignated miles between them.

programs.label: Alaska Scenic Byways Program
programs.issuer: Alaska Department of Transportation and Public Facilities

members.name: Alaska Marine Highway: Inside Passage Routes
members.blurb: State ferries work up the Inside Passage from British Columbia to Skagway, sheltered from the open Pacific by some 1,500 islands, calling at Wrangell's petroglyph beach and at Petersburg, which calls itself Little Norway.
members.note: Shown on the map as Alaska's Marine Highway.

members.name: Alaska Railroad
members.blurb: The railroad's main line runs about 470 miles from tidewater at Seward to Fairbanks, crossing Hurricane Gulch on the way, and its trains still stop for anyone flagging them down beside the track.

members.name: Copper River Highway
members.blurb: From Cordova the highway follows the old copper railroad grade across the Copper River Delta, a stopover for shorebirds by the hundreds of thousands. A washed-out bridge at Mile 36 now stops cars short of the Million Dollar Bridge.

members.name: Dalton Highway
members.blurb: A gravel haul road built for the pipeline, the Dalton runs 414 miles from the Elliott Highway to Deadhorse, crossing the Yukon River and the Arctic Circle and topping Atigun Pass in the Brooks Range at 4,800 feet.

members.name: Glenn Highway
members.blurb: From Anchorage the Glenn passes Palmer's 1935 colony farms and climbs the braided Matanuska River past the Matanuska Glacier to Eureka Summit, where four mountain ranges are in view at once.

members.name: Haines Highway
members.blurb: The Haines Highway climbs the Chilkat River valley toward the Yukon border on a path first used by the Chilkat, past cottonwood flats where more than 3,500 bald eagles gather in late fall to feed on spawning salmon.

members.name: Kachemak Bay Route
members.blurb: A boat route from the Homer Spit across Kachemak Bay to Seldovia, close under Gull Island's nesting seabirds, with sea otters in the shallows and the volcanoes Augustine and Redoubt across seventy miles of open water.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Parks Highway
members.blurb: Through Denali State Park and on to Healy, the Parks Highway passes Byers Lake and the Hurricane Gulch bridge, tops Broad Pass at 2,400 feet and runs by the road into Denali National Park.

members.name: Prince of Wales Island Road System
members.blurb: Paved roads wind through Tongass rainforest from the Hollis ferry landing to the island's small towns, with totem parks at Klawock and Hydaburg and gravel spurs leading north toward the karst caves at El Capitan.

members.name: Richardson Highway: north segment
members.blurb: The north end of Alaska's oldest highway, a gold rush trail turned wagon road, runs from Delta Junction to Fairbanks by way of Rika's Roadhouse at Big Delta and the 42-foot Santa at North Pole.

members.name: Seward Highway
members.blurb: The Seward Highway runs its first 50 miles along Turnagain Arm, where beluga whales surface off ghost stands of spruce drowned by salt water in the 1964 earthquake, then climbs past Summit Lake and Moose Pass to Seward.

members.name: Steese Highway
members.blurb: Out of Fairbanks past the five-deck Gold Dredge Number 8, the Steese turns to gravel near the mining town of Central and ends at Circle on the Yukon, a town once wrongly believed to sit on the Arctic Circle.

members.name: Sterling Highway: north segment
members.blurb: Leaving the Seward Highway at Tern Lake, the Sterling runs beside blue-green Kenai Lake to Cooper Landing and follows the Kenai River, a sportfishing water where the Russian River comes in, to the Skilak Lake Road.

members.name: Taylor & Top of the World Highways
members.blurb: Narrow and mostly gravel, the Taylor leaves the Alaska Highway at Tetlin Junction for the Fortymile goldfields and Chicken, named by settlers who could not spell ptarmigan, then joins the Top of the World Highway for the Yukon border.

members.name: Walden Point Road
members.blurb: Walden Point Road runs 14.7 miles along the shore of Annette Island from Annette Bay to Metlakatla, home of the Metlakatla Indian Community, past waterfalls and muskeg where Sitka black-tailed deer are a common sight.
